idiom_name: no pattern syntax: tag switch + destructuring with a throwing default
alternative: Model the variants as a TypeScript discriminated union and let an assertNever (never) arm prove coverage at build time (see pattern-matching.typescript.json); for runtime-only code use the ts-pattern library's match().with(...).exhaustive(), or a tag-keyed handler table whose default entry throws.
implementation_notes: JavaScript has destructuring and switch but no match expression: a switch on a discriminant plus object destructuring can bind the payload (const { x, y } = event), yet nothing checks that every variant is handled - the TC39 pattern-matching proposal is still at stage 1, no engine ships it, and a missing case is a silent no-op. Plain JavaScript therefore cannot deliver the pattern's payoff, compile-time totality, which is why it is discouraged for this decision: move the check to the type layer (TypeScript discriminated unions with assertNever, or // @ts-check with JSDoc typedefs) or to a checked runtime library such as ts-pattern. A bare tag switch stays acceptable for genuinely open dispatch as long as its default arm throws, so a new variant fails loudly at the dispatch site.
pitfalls: A switch without a default silently does nothing for an unhandled variant, so the bug appears downstream rather than at the dispatch site.
Destructuring turns a missing payload field into undefined instead of an error; validate or type the shape before matching it.
Matching is structural, not nominal: an extra field changes nothing, while a renamed discriminant value silently routes the variant to default.
